s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with chest pain and ECG changes
salient_findings: Dull chest pain of 2 hours' duration
ST segment depression >1mm in V2 and V3
New discordant ST elevation of 1mm in leads II, III, and aVF
key_facts: Male patient in his 70s
History of coronary artery bypass surgery
Ejection fraction of 25%
Biventricular pacemaker placement
Chest pain duration of 2 hours
ECG shows sinus activity at 72 beats/min
QRS duration of 160 milliseconds
Ventricular depolarization preceded by 2 pacing stimuli
Initial troponin negative 2 hours after symptom onset
Cardiac catheterization revealed thrombotic occlusion of saphenous vein graft
Occlusive lesions in proximal obtuse marginal artery

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of coronary artery bypass surgery and the cardiac catheterization revealed thrombotic occlusion of the saphenous vein graft, which is consistent with graft occlusion as the cause of the patient's symptoms

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Initial troponin was negative 2 hours after symptom onset, which makes acute myocardial infarction less likely

rejected.label: Unstable angina
rejected.why: The ECG changes and the cardiac catheterization findings suggest a more severe condition than unstable angina

rejected.label: Saphenous vein graft disease
rejected.why: While the patient does have saphenous vein graft disease, the more specific and immediate cause of the symptoms is the graft occlusion

rejected.label: Native coronary artery disease
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and the cardiac catheterization findings are more directly related to the graft occlusion than to native coronary artery disease
